annotation.title_clean: Integrating Ethics and Engineering in Practice: Outcomes from the 2025 AI, Robotics, & Ethics Summer Camp
annotation.title_en: Integrating Ethics and Engineering in Practice: Outcomes from the 2025 AI, Robotics, & Ethics Summer Camp
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Slaton, W.; Zhang, L.; Butler, J.
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper reporting the second AI, Robotics & Ethics Summer Camp at the University of Central Arkansas, where high schoolers built autonomous BearCar robots and studied ethics. Pre/post tests with 20 campers show statistically significant gains in engineering and ethics knowledge. It is an educational study, not a governance document.
key_provisions_or_claims: Residential camp combined building autonomous BearCar robots with ethics theory, Ethics Bowl cases and films.
80% of 20 campers improved overall on pre/post tests.
Ethics gains significant (Wilcoxon p=0.0033); engineering gains significant (paired t-test p=0.00047).
Self-driving ethical dilemmas were embedded in the training track through penalized human and animal figurines.
Hardware and software upgrades, including a watchdog timer, improved safety and ease of assembly.
